suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-23 adds this relationship only as a bounded vestibular-schwannoma hearing-loss association. The cited natural-history study describes hearing decline in sporadic vestibular schwannoma, but it does not establish that any individual's hearing loss was caused by an acoustic neuroma or exclude presbycusis, noise exposure, ototoxic medication, middle-ear disease, congenital loss, treatment effects, or other causes. Require documented acoustic neuroma/vestibular schwannoma, separately established hearing loss by audiometry, compatible laterality and chronology, and review of tumor, auditory-nerve, treatment, and competing-ear findings. Do not infer hearing loss from the tumor diagnosis, tinnitus, imbalance, or subjective difficulty without objective audiologic testing.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of acoustic neuroma/vestibular schwannoma and hearing loss
Serial pure-tone audiometry, speech discrimination, and laterality identifying the type and course of loss
MRI tumor location, size, growth, internal auditory canal involvement, and specialist findings
Chronology of tumor discovery, hearing change, observation, surgery, radiation, and other treatment

Resolution of publication guard: Require documented vestibular schwannoma, objective hearing loss, compatible laterality/chronology, and tumor/treatment review; do not infer loss from tumor history alone.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The cited review describes hearing decline as part of the natural history of sporadic vestibular schwannoma, supporting focused neurotologic and audiologic review without establishing deterministic individual causation.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established by the current evidence; objective audiology, tumor anatomy, laterality, chronology, treatment, and competing causes are required for individual review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A vestibular schwannoma may affect the cochlear nerve or inner-ear auditory pathway and contribute to hearing decline, but the individual mechanism remains hypothesized until tumor anatomy, laterality, chronology, and objective audiology are correlated.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The cited review addresses hearing-loss natural history in sporadic vestibular schwannoma but does not prove that an individual's hearing loss was caused by acoustic neuroma; objective testing, tumor correlation, treatment review, and alternative causes are required.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent tumor and audiologic diagnoses; serial ear-specific audiometry; MRI and specialist findings; chronology; treatment history; and assessment of age-related, noise-related, ototoxic, middle-ear, congenital, and other causes.
